findings: F1-75-l3-gating: "peripherals start with their clocks off" -> chip-specific: RP2350 clock enables reset to on and peripherals are held in reset until released (D8 §8.1.3.5, §7.5.1)
F1-75-hardware: RC oscillator "trimmed at the factory" -> frequency varies with PVT; RP2350 ROSC nominal 11 MHz, guaranteed 4.6–19.6 MHz (D8 §8.1.2.2)
F1-75-hardware: clock gate = logic gate plus latch -> glitch-free switching via glitchless multiplexer and dividers that synchronise their enable (D8 §8.1.3.2, §8.1.3.3)
F1-75-hardware: prescaler toggles every N/2 input cycles -> one output cycle per N input cycles (D8 §8.1.3.3)

F1-75-l3-emulator: RCC/GPIOC offsets, bit 4 and value 0x11 from memory (unverified box) -> confirmed against ST's headers: APB2ENR at 0x18, IOPCEN bit 4, CRH 0x04, ODR 0x0C, 0x11 = output 10 MHz push-pull on pins 8 and 9 (D9)
F1-75-l2-registers: status bits cleared "by writing 0" -> replaced by documented rules: write-1-to-clear (CMSDK, RP2350 WC), clear-on-read (SysTick), FIFO read (D10 Table 4-7; D8 App. A; D11 B3.3.3)

F1-75-l2-clocks: generic start-up clock sequence incl. flash wait states -> RP2350 sequence (XOSC_STABLE, PLL LOCK, glitchless switch); flash wait states moved to box (D8 §8.1.2.3, §8.1.2.6, §8.1.3.2)
F1-75-l2-baud: receiver tolerates "a few percent at most" -> moved to an unverified box; 2 % labelled as an exercise value (not found)
F1-75-jargon: gated peripheral "registers cannot be written on many chips" -> what its registers do is chip-specific (D8 §8.1.3.5)
unverified: F1-75-l2-baud: UART receiver tolerance to baud mismatch
unverified: F1-75-hardware: reset values of STM32F1 clock enables; STM32 flash wait states before a faster clock
